title: Longer Grace Period for Some Car Parks with Electronic Parking Systems during Peak Hours
what_it_is: Longer Grace Period for Some Car Parks with Electronic Parking Systems during Peak Hours

sections.label: HDB URA car park charges
sections.summary: HDB and URA impose charges after the grace period to ensure quick vehicle turnover and prevent congestion in car parks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: HDB and URA need to impose charges after the grace period to ensure quick turnover of vehicles in the car park.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: This prevents build-up of congestion in the car park, allows more motorists to make use of the car park and ensures that the interests of residents who drive or have season parking are adequately taken care of.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, as parking charges in car parks with EPS are levied on a per-minute basis, if motorists exceed the grace period, they only need to pay for the actual duration of their parking in that car park.

sections.label: Grace period balance for users
sections.summary: The grace period alone will not solve the issue, as a uniform grace period balances different car park users.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The grace period in and of itself will not solve the issue that the Member has highlighted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: As I have said earlier, the reason why we set a uniform grace period is to strike a balance between the different users of the car park.

sections.label: EPS car parks consistency and design
sections.summary: With over 1,500 EPS car parks, certainty and consistency are essential, and issues in estates relate mainly to pick-up and drop-off point design.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Bearing in mind also that we have more than 1,500 car parks under the EPS system, as mentioned in my earlier Parliamentary Question reply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And so, some amount of certainty, predictability and consistency is essential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Nevertheless, if there is an issue in particular estates, as I had said earlier, it is not primarily the grace period, I think it has got to do with the design of the pick-up and drop-off points.
